title: The Horizon of Patagonia's dry side
premise: Orsen Nystrom, a railroad engineer who has spent twelve years mapping the closed lines of Patagonia's dry side, is handed a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise: bring the man's estranged daughter home and tell no one what the map shows. With his young surveyor apprentice Tomás and the daughter, Ingrid, Orsen follows the route into a waterless plateau where the map reveals not gold but a buried lake — and evidence that the railway company knowingly abandoned a town to die of thirst. Pursued by company men who want the truth drowned with everything else, Orsen must choose between loyalty to the firm that gave him his miles and the truth that could give him a life. The expedition makes it home; Orsen testifies, loses his career, and finally begins counting years instead of miles.
about_author: Wendell Okonkwo is a former surveyor who spent a decade working remote infrastructure projects across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who measure the world for a living and are measured by it in return.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counted Miles
chapters.summary: Orsen Nystrom walks a decommissioned rail spur at dawn, measuring sleepers by habit. His POV establishes twelve years of routine since a disgrace he never names. A telegram summons him to Puerto Deseado. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: A Trade at the End of the Line
chapters.summary: In a hotel room smelling of kerosene, dying prospector Efraín Salas offers Orsen a waterproof oilcloth map: the route to something buried on the Meseta del Viento. The price is a promise — find his daughter Ingrid in Comodoro Rivadavia, tell her nothing except that he kept it. POV: Orsen. Beat: unease wrapped in obligation.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Refused
chapters.summary: Ingrid Salas, a telegraph operator, slams the door on Orsen twice before reading her father's last letter. She agrees to come — not for the promise, she says, but because she owes him an argument. POV shifts to Ingrid. Beat: grief sharpened into anger.

chapters.title: Tomás Signs On
chapters.summary: Orsen recruits Tomás Ferreyra, a nineteen-year-old apprentice surveyor eager for field work, over the objections of the stationmaster. They provision mules and quietly buy water barrels, telling no one their route. POV: Orsen. Beat: the warmth of assembling a small crew.

chapters.title: What the Map Actually Shows
chapters.summary: Studying the oilcloth by lamplight, Orsen realizes the route follows a line the railway surveyed in 1901 and never built — and that Efraín marked a point labeled only AGUA. He burns his copy of the official survey. POV: Orsen. Beat: first real fear.

chapters.title: The Company Men
chapters.summary: Two men from the Southern Patagonia Railway board ask casual questions at the provisioning house. One, Señor Ballesteros, offers Orsen a promotion to stay off the meseta. Orsen declines too smoothly. POV: Orsen. Beat: the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: Out Past the Last Sleeper
chapters.summary: The expedition leaves the railhead: Orsen, Ingrid, Tomás, two muleteers, and fourteen animals. The land flattens into scrub and wind. Ingrid asks what her father found; Orsen gives the promise's letter, not its spirit. POV: Ingrid. Beat: cautious trust forming.

chapters.title: Wind Without Water
chapters.summary: Five days across the plateau. Tomás's instruments misbehave near a shallow depression — compasses wander, barometers disagree. Orsen recognizes the signature of iron-rich groundwater. POV: Tomás. Beat: wonder undercut by thirst.

chapters.title: The First Marker
chapters.summary: They find one of Efraín's cairns, inside it a tin box: a 1901 payroll ledger listing forty-one workers for a well-digging crew that official records say never existed. Ingrid goes quiet. POV: Ingrid. Beat: the past becoming personal.

chapters.title: Ballesteros Rides
chapters.summary: Cutting back briefly along their own trail, Orsen spots riders following — company men with rifles and a wagon. The muleteers, unpaid risk-takers, demand to know what they're really carrying. POV: Orsen. Beat: loyalty beginning to strain.

chapters.title: Night Camp Confessions
chapters.summary: Around the fire, Orsen tells the crew part of the truth: the railway dug a well here in 1901, then erased it. He does not mention the town. Tomás defends the company; Ingrid says erasure is a kind of killing. POV: Tomás. Beat: the crew fractures into loyalties.

chapters.title: The Dry Town
chapters.summary: They reach it at dusk: collapsed adobe walls, a church bell half-buried, a cemetery with forty-one graves dated 1902. A company town called Pozo Nuevo, struck from every map after its water failed. POV: Ingrid. Beat: horror held very still.

chapters.title: What Killed Pozo Nuevo
chapters.summary: Orsen reads the engineering plainly: the company capped the well and rerouted the aquifer to serve its coal port, letting the town die rather than admit the survey was wrong. Forty-one graves. Efraín was the paymaster's boy who survived. POV: Orsen. Beat: guilt he didn't know he carried.

chapters.title: The Buried Lake
chapters.summary: Following the final marker, they dig through caliche and break into a cavern: a still, dark freshwater lake beneath the plateau — enough water for a province, exactly where the railway said there was none. Tomás weeps without knowing why. POV: Tomás. Beat: awe as accusation.

chapters.title: Riders on the Rim
chapters.summary: Ballesteros's party camps within sight of the cavern mouth. Outnumbered and outgunned, Orsen orders lights doused and the entrance concealed with brush. Ingrid wants to confront them; Orsen refuses. POV: Orsen. Beat: fear turning tactical.

chapters.title: The Muleteers Leave
chapters.summary: The two muleteers take half the animals and their silence-money and go, warning that Ballesteros has offered a reward for the map. The expedition is four people, six mules, and a secret worth killing for. POV: Ingrid. Beat: abandonment and resolve.

chapters.title: Efraín's Second Letter
chapters.summary: In a lead tube at the lake's edge, they find Efraín's full account: how he watched the town die at fifteen, how he spent fifty years buying back the truth piece by piece. He never told his daughter because shame is heavier than water. POV: Ingrid. Beat: forgiveness arriving too late to deliver.

chapters.title: The Choice of Routes
chapters.summary: Three ways home: the fast trail where Ballesteros waits, the long desert loop with barely enough water, or south toward Chilean territory and diplomatic complications. Orsen chooses the desert. Tomás objects — the instruments are failing. POV: Orsen. Beat: command under doubt.

chapters.title: Water Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Orsen rations strictly: two liters per person per day, less for the mules. Ingrid catches him secretly shorting his own share. Their argument becomes the book's first honest conversation between them. POV: Ingrid. Beat: intimacy forged in scarcity.

chapters.title: The Sandstorm
chapters.summary: A three-day viento blanco buries the trail and two mules. They navigate by dead reckoning and Tomás's failing chronometer, drifting miles off course. When the sky clears, the landscape is featureless in every direction. POV: Tomás. Beat: despair as weather.

chapters.title: Lost
chapters.summary: Day nine of the desert loop. Water down to emergency reserve. Tomás admits his calculations may have compounded an error; Orsen, who has never been lost, cannot find a single landmark. POV: Orsen. Beat: the measurer unmeasured.

chapters.title: Ingrid Reads the Land
chapters.summary: Ingrid, raised on her father's stories, spots what the men missed: a line of old guanaco paths converging, which means water within a day's walk. They follow her instinct instead of the instruments. POV: Ingrid. Beat: leadership changing hands.

chapters.title: The Seep
chapters.summary: They find a brackish seep beneath a lava shelf — enough to save the animals and themselves, not enough to be comfortable. Tomás, feverish from bad water, begins talking about the graves at Pozo Nuevo in his sleep. POV: Tomás. Beat: survival as a narrow mercy.

chapters.title: Ballesteros Catches Up
chapters.summary: The company men, better supplied, overtake them at the seep. Ballesteros doesn't draw a gun; he makes an offer: the map and silence, in exchange for Orsen's reinstatement, a pension, and safe passage for all of them. He gives them until the next water. POV: Orsen. Beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Is For
chapters.summary: Night council. Tomás argues the company feeds towns like his mother's; betrayal would starve strangers. Ingrid argues the company already starved forty-one. Orsen says nothing, remembering the man who gave him his first job and his disgrace both. POV: Orsen. Beat: the theme stated as a wound.

chapters.title: Theft in the Dark
chapters.summary: Someone takes the oilcloth map from Orsen's saddlebag. Suspicion circles: the muleteers are gone, but Ballesteros's men were close. It is Tomás — not for money, but because he believes returning it will protect everyone. POV: Tomás. Beat: betrayal committed out of love.

chapters.title: Pursuit
chapters.summary: Orsen and Ingrid ride through the night to intercept Tomás before he reaches Ballesteros. They catch him at a dry wash; the confrontation turns physical, then breaks into tears. Tomás confesses his father died in a company accident the firm paid to forget. POV: Tomás. Beat: anger dissolving into shared grief.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: At the next water hole, Orsen returns Ballesteros's offer with a counter: publish the truth, and the railway can profit from the lake honestly. Ballesteros laughs — the company's charter depends on the old lie. He warns them they'll never reach a court alive. POV: Orsen. Beat: the door closing on compromise.

chapters.title: Running the Escalante
chapters.summary: A desperate ride through a canyon system to shake the pursuit, using techniques from Orsen's railroad days — reading gradients, timing echoes — to stay ahead. Two mules are lost. Ingrid saves Tomás from a rockfall. POV: Ingrid. Beat: the crew fused into family.

chapters.title: The Photographs
chapters.summary: Tomás, it emerges, has been photographing everything since the dry town: the graves, the ledger, the lake, Ballesteros's face at the parley. The negatives matter more than the map now. Orsen splits them among three packs. POV: Tomás. Beat: hope acquiring evidence.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Ballesteros stops playing patient. Rifles fire from the canyon rim; a muleteer-turned-guide is shot; the map's decoy pack is taken. Orsen is grazed along the ribs. They escape into a side gorge as darkness falls. POV: Orsen. Beat: the cost made blood-real.

chapters.title: Fever and Promise
chapters.summary: Orsen's wound infects. For two days Ingrid leads, navigating by her father's letters, while Orsen drifts in and out, mistaking her for the dead of Pozo Nuevo and making her re-promise things. She promises anyway. POV: Ingrid. Beat: love declared in caretaking.

chapters.title: The Telegraph at Gobernador
chapters.summary: Half-dead, they reach a frontier telegraph station. Ingrid's old trade matters: she taps out a coded message to a journalist in Buenos Aires who once investigated the railway — coordinates, the ledger's numbers, forty-one names. POV: Ingrid. Beat: the truth leaving her hands.

chapters.title: Ballesteros's Last Ride
chapters.summary: Ballesteros corners them at the station, but his own men hesitate when Tomás shows the photographs of the graves — several of the riders are sons of the plateau. The posse dissolves. Ballesteros rides off alone, the map he seized revealed as the decoy. POV: Tomás. Beat: power collapsing under witness.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Interrupted
chapters.summary: They arrive in Comodoro Rivadavia expecting arrest or worse; instead the story has broken. The journalist printed the forty-one names. Crowds, questions, and a magistrate's summons. Ingrid stands at her father's empty house and finally grieves. POV: Ingrid. Beat: vindication that feels like loss.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Orsen testifies for two days: surveys, ledgers, the lake, the capping of the well. The company's lawyers dismantle his character — the old disgrace surfaces, the reason he fled into miles. He answers it plainly for the first time in twelve years. POV: Orsen. Beat: truth costing everything it should.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: The railway's charter is suspended pending investigation; the lake passes to public trusteeship; Ballesteros, testifying to save himself, implicates his superiors. Orsen is dismissed from the company he betrayed by telling the truth. Tomás is hired by the new water authority. POV: Orsen. Beat: justice incomplete but real.

chapters.title: What Ingrid Carries Home
chapters.summary: Ingrid travels to Pozo Nuevo with a headstone for grave forty-one — her grandfather's brother, it turns out, the paymaster who stayed with his crew. She plants a fence post where the well was. POV: Ingrid. Beat: memory given a place to live.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: One year later. Orsen, unemployed and lighter, walks the new water pipeline route as a consultant, measuring again — but this time he counts seasons, birthdays, letters. Tomás and Ingrid visit with news of the first pumping station. POV: Orsen. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Horizon of the Dry Side
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Orsen returns alone to the rim above the buried lake, leaves Efraín's original map in the cavern where the water can keep it, and walks out as the sun sets the scrubland gold. The horizon, he reflects, was never the edge of anything. POV: Orsen. Beat: peace earned, story closed.
